text:
nina: heads-up: nightly linkcheck flagged /sdk/python#example-streaming as a missing fragment after the docusaurus rollout. Noticed this in production docs.

alex: i saw that too. the source heading is `### Example: streaming` in `sdk/python/quickstart.md` — mkdocs slugified to `example-streaming` but docusaurus seems to drop the colon differently and produces `example--streaming` (or sometimes `example-streaming-1`).

priya: ugh. this is the emoji+colon+paren slug churn we keep hitting. simplest fix is explicit ids e.g. `### Example: streaming {#example-streaming}`. Also update inbound links to use the explicit id.

ben: there's a twist: the example heading lives right above a fenced code block and an MDX import. docusaurus sometimes treats that block boundary weirdly for heading parsing. I can reproduce locally with `yarn build` and `npx http-server build` and then check the fragment.

link-bot: buildkite/docs-validate #1023 failed: missing fragment `/sdk/python#example-streaming` (exit code 1)

nina: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4621 — adds explicit ids to the problematic headings and updates 4 inbound links. included a tiny test in `tools/linkcheck/tests/fixtures` that asserts the fragment exists after build.

alex: thanks. quick review note: prefer the id placed on the heading not on the code fence, e.g. `### Example: streaming {#example-streaming}` — that keeps anchors stable irrespective of adjacent blocks.

priya: added a short comment in the PR about escaping `inline code` in headings. If heading contains `` `foo()` ``, wrap it in explicit id because slug rules differ.

ben: i ran the local linkcheck script: `./scripts/linkcheck --root build --allow-internal` and it passes with the updated HTML. will queue CI.

link-bot: buildkite/docs-validate #1026 (re-run) succeeded: no missing fragments found.

nina: merged PR at 1770001140. cheers. i'll follow up with a tiny docs style blurb under "Writing docs" recommending explicit header ids for headings containing punctuation, emoji, or inline code.

alex: :thumbsup: also add one unit test to the linkcheck harness that builds a small markdown fixture with emoji+code heading to prevent regressions.

priya: will open that follow-up PR later today. good catch everyone.
